name: Conditional Content Block – AI Citation Optimizer
author: Mainul Kabir Aion

sections.description:
Conditional Content Block – AI Citation Optimizer helps you do two important jobs inside the WordPress editor:

  • control which visitors see specific content blocks
  • improve public-facing content so it is easier for AI systems and readers to understand, extract, and cite

This makes the plugin especially useful for publishers, marketers, SEO teams, agencies, membership sites, course creators, and content teams that need both audience targeting and AI-ready content structure.

Suggested Google title:
Conditional Content Block: AI Citation Optimizer & Smart Content Visibility

Why use this plugin?

  • Keep personalized or gated content inside conditional blocks
  • Keep Quick Answer and FAQ content public when visibility matters
  • Improve AI citation readiness before publishing
  • Add answer-focused content blocks directly in Gutenberg
  • Catch structural issues like weak intros, long paragraphs, missing tables, and thin extractability

Built for these use cases

  • AI SEO and answer engine optimization
  • AI-ready blog posts and tutorials
  • FAQ and quick answer content strategies
  • membership or lead-generation content with public summaries
  • editorial QA before content goes live

Features:
– Backward-compatible Conditional Content block
– Smart visibility rules for logged-in users, logged-out users, roles, device targeting, and schedules
– AI Citation Optimizer sidebar inside Gutenberg
– Citation score and citation probability analysis
– AI Quick Answer block with generate, regenerate, and manual editing
– AI FAQ block with AI-assisted question and answer generation
– Extractability analyzer for long paragraphs
– Visibility-aware warnings when key answer content is hidden inside conditional blocks
– AI quick fixes for article tables and paragraph rewrites
– OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and WordPress core connector support
– Provider-aware settings with direct API key links
– Cached analysis results for performance

sections.installation:
1. Upload the conditional-content-block folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  3. Configure AI provider settings in Settings > Conditional Content Block
  4. Add the “Conditional Content”, “AI Quick Answer”, or “AI FAQ” block in the editor
  5. Use the AI Citation Optimizer sidebar to analyze content on demand
sections.faq:
Does this remove the original conditional content functionality?

No. The original conditional content block remains available and backward compatible.

Which AI providers are supported?

OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini are supported through the plugin settings page.

Can I use the optimizer without an AI provider?

Yes. The rule-based scoring engine works without any AI connection. AI integration is optional.

Can I still use this as a normal conditional content plugin?

Yes. The original conditional visibility workflow remains part of the plugin and stays backward compatible with existing content.

Where should I place the AI Quick Answer and AI FAQ blocks?

For best results, place the AI Quick Answer near the top of the article. The AI FAQ block works best near the end of the post as a follow-up section.

What is the plugin optimizing for?

The plugin is designed for AI citation readiness, answer engine optimization, extractable formatting, FAQ coverage, and stronger content structure inside Gutenberg.

What does the citation score evaluate?

It checks structure, quick answers, FAQ coverage, heading hierarchy, intro length, paragraph extractability, tables, and optional AI guidance.

Can hidden content affect AI citation visibility?

Yes. If your most important answer content is restricted inside a conditional block, public visitors and AI systems may not see it. The optimizer warns about this.

Where are analysis results stored?

The latest analysis is cached in post meta and recalculated only when the content changes or the editor requests a new analysis.
